analysis:
This batch changes only offline test scripts; no workflow, resolver or verify_workflow_source implementation source is supplied.

scripts/test-provider-release-resolution.py (head 43-106, 147-174) pins the new routing:
- A dispatched dev lane resolves only as a validation build with publish=false; a dev publication without a dev push fails closed.
- A master push publishes staging only; dev and prod from master fail closed.
- A dev push publishes dev only, versioned -dev.branch.N; prod, staging and empty environments fail closed.
- Dev from devx, dev/x or candidate refs is refused.
- Injection cases still emit no outputs.

scripts/test-provider-release-resume.py (head 41, 50-51, 135-173) adds a dev-push source test. It expects a GitHub-verified commit on dev-branch ancestry, environment dev only, and no substitution of dev ancestry for master ancestry.

This is new attack surface relative to the base, where the only branch-push route was master ancestry. A dev push now reaches the reusable release-provider.yml. Per the test-release-dev-branch.py docstring, that path uses Developer ID signing, notarization and DEV_* secrets.

This matters for the threat model:
- Dev-branch write access, not reviewed master, now controls a signed, notarized dev-coordinator artifact.
- This is relevant to A-011/A-017 and T-013/T-054.
- These tests assert only dev-coordinator scope, not prod.

Integration must verify:
- release-provider.yml and resolve-provider-release.sh enforce these routes.
- provider_release_resume/api.py checks dev ancestry against refs/heads/dev.
- Branch protection exists on dev.
- The Developer ID / notarization secrets exposed to dev pushes cannot yield artifacts that the prod or staging qualification (A-017) accepts. The same Apple team identity is a concern.
- The test-release-dev-branch.py content was not supplied (metadata only), so its claimed pins (no ad-hoc signing, secrets: inherit, fan-helper requirement) are unverified.

No concrete regression is visible in the test code itself.
